titleEn: Livestock methane reduction: Brazilian beef pilot generates first inset credits via Athian
titleZh: 巴西牛肉试点项目通过Athian平台产生首批内插信用，助力畜牧业甲烷减排
summaryZh: 美国公司Athian与澳大利亚甲烷减排专家Rumin8及巴西牛肉出口商Minerva Foods合作，在巴西牛肉供应链中完成首个内插信用（inset credits）试点。该项目验证了Rumin8饲料添加剂可使甲烷排放减少50.4%，并提高饲料转化率5%。Athian通过其平台完成数据验证、信用注册和销售，展示了内插模式在国际畜牧系统中的可行性，为食品企业实现Scope 3减排目标提供了新路径。
featuredReason: 该新闻展示了内插信用机制在牛肉供应链中的首次应用，结合了饲料添加剂技术、数据验证平台和供应链金融，为智慧畜牧从业者提供了如何将减排技术转化为可交易资产的实践案例。
contentFull:
Athian has sold the first inset credits generated by a Brazilian beef project following a pilot with Australia-based methane-reduction specialist Rumin8 and Minerva Foods, the leading exporter of beef in South America.

Rather than buying carbon offsets from projects outside their value chains, Minerva and other food companies are increasingly looking to purchase insets: credits generated by emissions reductions within their own supply chains.

Typically, says Indiana-based Athian, “A large food company provides financial incentives for farmers to make a practice change, and we facilitate that process.”

The firm, which is best-known for its work in US dairy cattle but is also working with partners in Australia and other markets, used its insetting framework and platform to facilitate data verification, register the resulting credits and sell them to Minerva Foods.

The 120-day pilot assessed both Rumin8’s performance and its potential to form the basis of a future protocol on Athian’s platform. According to Rumin8, cattle receiving the additive in a total mixed ration produced 50.4% less methane and achieved a 5% improvement in feed conversion efficiency compared with cattle fed the same diet without it.

“We not only proved the insetting process, from the generation and verification of reductions to their sale as Scope 3 assets, for the first time in Brazilian beef,” said Athian cofounder Kendra Tolley. “We also demonstrated how Athian’s approach applies internationally and across livestock systems.”

Founded in 2022, Athian works with livestock producers on GHG emission reduction strategies from feed ingredients to manure management; facilitates secure data collection via its software platform for third-party review and verification; and registers and sells outcomes as inset credits to food companies looking to cut Scope 3 emissions to meet ESG goals.

“We believe environmental progress in beef has to be measurable and verifiable,” said Minerva global sustainability director Marta Giannichi. “This pilot demonstrates that it’s possible to quantify methane reductions at the farm level and integrate them into a credible supply chain framework.”

Insetting vs offsetting

While there has been some recent backsliding on ESG goals from large food companies, most global food companies remain committed to reducing Scope 3 emissions and are increasingly looking to projects in their own supply chains rather than offsets, claimed Tolley.

This is in part because they can also deliver broader benefits beyond emissions reductions from more resilient supply chains, improved water quality or improved operational efficiency on the farm, to increased productivity (feed conversion rates) in the case of the project with Rumin8, she said.

“Companies are just being more strategic about what projects to invest in.”

That said, it’s still relatively early days for some of the technologies in question when it comes to livestock methane reduction, she acknowledged, with new technologies and approaches still going through regulatory processes that can differ widely from country to country.

In the US, for example, Athian has been working closely with farmers that use methane-busting feed additive Bovaer from dsm Firmenich via Elanco, the approval process for which took several years, said Tolley.

“We have about eight protocols on our platform that we support through US dairy, and we have engaged in activities covering about 10% of the dairy cows in the US. We have multiple contractual agreements with large food companies that are relying on us to provide their scope three reduction goals.”

The key is making the process credible and defensible for food companies but easy for farmers to participate and upload data, she added. “One of the problems we’re really trying to solve is that many food companies have been doing this as bespoke projects they were managing internally.”

Athian’s board features experts in enteric and manure methane that review all of the methodologies it brings onto the platform to ensure the science is credible, claimed Tolley. “We then have that protocol or methodology reviewed by a third party to ensure we are complying with our own governance structure as well as external standards, ISO standards, and Greenhouse Gas Protocol standards.”

Rumin8: a portfolio of offerings

Rumin8 is developing a variety of feed supplements that reduce enteric methane production from cow burps, a leading source of GHG emissions.

Its flagship product—which cofounder David Messina says he hopes will secure regulatory approval in Brazil next year followed by other markets including New Zealand, Australia, the US, and Europe—is a granule containing a stabilized form of bromoform that can be added to whole mix rations and supplement mixes for cattle.

“We can now do 3.5 million doses a day with a single manufacturing train in a GMP environment and that can scale to 8-9 million quite quickly.” said Messina.

Other products under development include a slow-release bolus that could deliver active ingredients to the cattle rumen over time, a compound that converts to bromoform in the cattle rumen post ingestion, and a fungi-based platform that produces bromoform, said Messina.

“This looks like it could be a much cheaper way to produce pure bromoform than our GMP solution [which relies on synthetic chemistry].”

Co-claiming models for Scope 3 emission reductions

Ultimately, tech relying solely on carbon insetting or offsetting to deliver a return is risky, acknowledged Messina, who said the fact that Rumin8 products can also deliver a productivity benefit to the farmer has been key to its appeal.

However, new initiatives such as “co-claiming” models that allow multiple parties such as retailers, CPG companies and milk processors to spread the costs and rewards of insetting projects are helping reduce the burden on individual companies that have historically funded projects alone, said Messina.

“It means the whole financial burden doesn’t just sit with one participant in the supply chain.”

translationZh:
Athian已售出巴西牛肉项目产生的首批内插信用，该项目是与澳大利亚甲烷减排专家Rumin8及南美最大牛肉出口商Minerva Foods合作开展的试点。

与购买价值链外部项目的碳抵消不同，Minerva等食品公司越来越倾向于购买内插信用——即通过自身供应链内的减排活动产生的信用。

总部位于印第安纳州的Athian表示：“大型食品公司通常为农民提供经济激励，促使他们改变养殖实践，而我们负责促进这一过程。”该公司以服务美国奶牛业闻名，同时也与澳大利亚及其他市场的合作伙伴开展合作，其利用内插框架和平台促进数据验证、注册产生的信用，并将其出售给Minerva Foods。

这项为期120天的试点评估了Rumin8产品的性能，以及其未来在Athian平台上形成协议基础的潜力。据Rumin8称，与饲喂相同日粮但未添加该添加剂的牛相比，接受全混合日粮中添加剂的牛甲烷排放量减少了50.4%，饲料转化效率提高了5%。

Athian联合创始人肯德拉·托利表示：“我们不仅首次在巴西牛肉中证明了内插流程——从减排量的产生和验证到作为Scope 3资产出售，还展示了Athian的方法如何在国际上以及跨畜牧系统中应用。”

Athian成立于2022年，与畜牧生产者合作制定温室气体减排策略，涵盖从饲料原料到粪污管理；通过其软件平台促进安全数据收集，供第三方审查和验证；并将结果注册和出售为内插信用，提供给寻求削减Scope 3排放以实现ESG目标的食品公司。

Minerva全球可持续发展总监玛尔塔·贾尼基表示：“我们相信牛肉的环境进步必须是可测量和可验证的。这个试点表明，在农场层面量化甲烷减排并将其整合到可信的供应链框架中是可能的。”

**内插与抵消**

托利声称，尽管近期一些大型食品公司在ESG目标上有所退缩，但大多数全球食品公司仍致力于减少Scope 3排放，并越来越倾向于自身供应链内的项目，而非购买抵消。

她表示，部分原因在于这些项目除了减排外，还能带来更广泛的益处，如更具韧性的供应链、改善水质、提高农场运营效率，以及在与Rumin8合作的项目中提高生产力（饲料转化率）。

“公司正在更加战略性地选择投资项目。”

不过，她承认，在畜牧甲烷减排方面，某些技术仍处于早期阶段，新技术和方法仍在经历各国差异巨大的监管流程。

例如，在美国，Athian一直与使用帝斯曼芬美意（dsm-firmenich）通过Elanco销售的甲烷抑制饲料添加剂Bovaer的农民密切合作，该添加剂的审批过程耗时数年。

托利说：“我们的平台上有大约八个协议，支持美国奶牛业，我们参与的活动覆盖了美国约10%的奶牛。我们与多家大型食品公司签订了合同协议，它们依赖我们来实现其Scope 3减排目标。”

她补充说，关键是要使这一过程对食品公司可信且可辩护，同时让农民易于参与和上传数据。“我们真正试图解决的问题之一是，许多食品公司一直将这些作为内部管理的定制项目。”

托利称，Athian的董事会成员包括肠道和粪污甲烷领域的专家，他们审查平台上引入的所有方法学，以确保科学的可信度。“然后，我们会让第三方审查该协议或方法学，以确保我们符合自身的治理结构以及外部标准、ISO标准和温室气体议定书标准。”

**Rumin8：产品组合**

Rumin8正在开发多种饲料补充剂，以减少牛打嗝产生的肠道甲烷——这是温室气体排放的主要来源之一。

其旗舰产品是一种含有稳定形式溴仿的颗粒，可添加到牛的全混合日粮和补充剂混合物中。联合创始人大卫·梅西纳表示，他希望该产品能在明年获得巴西的监管批准，随后进入新西兰、澳大利亚、美国和欧洲等市场。

“我们现在可以在GMP环境下，通过单条生产线每天生产350万剂，并且可以很快扩大到800-900万剂。”梅西纳说。

梅西纳表示，其他正在开发的产品包括一种缓释瘤胃丸，可随时间向牛瘤胃输送活性成分；一种摄入后在牛瘤胃中转化为溴仿的化合物；以及一种基于真菌的生产溴仿的平台。

“这看起来可能是一种比我们的GMP解决方案（依赖合成化学）更便宜的生产纯溴仿的方法。”

**Scope 3减排的共同认领模式**

梅西纳承认，完全依赖碳内插或抵消来获得回报的技术存在风险，他表示，Rumin8产品还能为农民带来生产力效益，这是其吸引力的关键。

梅西纳表示，诸如“共同认领”模式等新举措，允许零售商、消费品公司和乳品加工商等多方分摊内插项目的成本和收益，有助于减轻历史上由单个公司独自承担项目的负担。

“这意味着整个财务负担不会只落在供应链中的一个参与者身上。”
author: Elaine Watson
